mbm-0393.clue: I keep the leather fish on dry land.
mbm-0393.quote: I stitched a scale pattern into a blue coin purse and gave it a bright brass eye. My niece feeds it pennies. So far it has been a wonderfully inexpensive pet.

mbm-0394.clue: My punch set has a potato stamp.
mbm-0394.quote: Before I try a new pattern in leather, I carve it in a potato and print it on paper. I liked one crooked leaf so much I copied the crooked line into the final belt.

mbm-0395.clue: I built a little light for the last line.
mbm-0395.quote: My computer draws a lamp in a window when I finish a page of my diary. I wrote the lamp code myself. Some nights I write two extra sentences just to see the windows upstairs light up too.

mbm-0396.clue: My club shoes are full of postcards.
mbm-0396.quote: I tuck a small club flyer into my shoebox after every great night out. I opened the box to polish my shoes and half a year of colored paper stars spilled across the floor.

mbm-0397.clue: I save the game at the flower cart.
mbm-0397.quote: There’s a cart of red flowers just past the hardest jump. I always let my character stand there a second before saving. My friend says I’ve given the little fellow a proper coffee break.

mbm-0398.clue: I can tell which paddle is my sister’s.
mbm-0398.quote: She painted a blackbird on the end and I painted a fish on mine. When we rest the paddles across the canoe, it looks like the bird is stalking our lunch.

mbm-0399.clue: I made the spoon its own balcony.
mbm-0399.quote: My soup bowl has a little clay ledge on one side. The spoon rests there without falling in. My brother calls it the best seat in the house and puts the spoon there between every bite.

mbm-0400.clue: My puppet takes very long naps.
mbm-0400.quote: I made a sleepy glove puppet with eyelids that drop when I tip my wrist. The children sing louder every time he nods off. Once the whole front row sang him to sleep in four different keys.

mbm-0401.clue: I sew summer into my winter coat.
mbm-0401.quote: I lined the pockets with scraps from a shirt I wore fishing. A tiny red sailboat peeks out if I pull the pockets inside out. In January the little boats get a lot of fresh air.

mbm-0402.clue: I cut the music around the trumpet.
mbm-0402.quote: For my uncle’s birthday banner I cut paper trumpets out of bright tissue. I left little curls in the gaps so the notes seemed to keep going after each trumpet ran out of paper.

mbm-0403.clue: I gave the accordion a little raincoat.
mbm-0403.quote: A shower passed over our vallenato circle and we kept the rhythm under a shop awning. Mum slipped the spare raincoat over my accordion case. The instrument and the melody both got home dry.

mbm-0404.clue: I bring a second straw hat for the peaches.
mbm-0404.quote: I buy peaches before I stretch out in the sun and keep them cool under a spare hat. My neighbor thought I’d brought a silent friend to the roof and nearly offered the peaches a chair.

mbm-0405.clue: I always volunteer to redraw the stumps.
mbm-0405.quote: We use sticks for our beach wicket but draw their shadows in the sand before play. When the shadows have completely moved away from the lines, everybody knows it’s time for lunch.

mbm-0406.clue: I carried the whole river in my shoe.
mbm-0406.quote: When we stepped out of the raft my water shoe squelched like a frog. I tipped it over and a smooth red pebble dropped into my palm. It’s in the bowl with my keys now.

mbm-0407.clue: I recognize my skis by the two suns.
mbm-0407.quote: My cousin and I painted a little orange sun on each tip. When I finally stayed upright through a long turn I could see both suns together ahead of me. It felt like a private sunrise.

mbm-0408.clue: I carry one orange for the last hill.
mbm-0408.quote: My running friend and I trade the orange halfway up, so we only have to carry it for half the climb. At the top we split it on the park bench. It tastes better than any medal I’ve won.

mbm-0409.clue: I crocheted a lid for the moon.
mbm-0409.quote: My niece’s round night-light looked too bright. I made a little crescent sleeve for it with open stitches. Her ceiling is now full of small stars that move whenever she turns the lamp.

mbm-0410.clue: I can hear the boat before I see it.
mbm-0410.quote: Our towboat’s bright yellow float squeaks against the dock. At first light that little squeak gets me into my vest faster than any alarm. My dad waves the float like a flag when my skis are ready.

mbm-0411.clue: I practice with the plainest envelope.
mbm-0411.quote: I learned to pull a bright paper butterfly from an empty envelope. The first one got caught on the flap and slowly unfolded anyway. I liked its sleepy entrance so much I still make it pause there.

mbm-0412.clue: I count the reeds at the last turn.
mbm-0412.quote: A patch of reeds beside my kayak route looks like a paintbrush dipped in gold. I waited there after sunset and watched the color slide down the stalks until just the tips were shining.

mbm-0413.clue: I put the spare button on the outside.
mbm-0413.quote: I sewed my brother a jacket and fastened its spare button right at the cuff in bright blue. He never has to look for it, and I can spot his wave all the way down the station platform.

mbm-0414.clue: I stitched the old well in circles.
mbm-0414.quote: Our family quilt shows the garden before the well was covered. I stitched rings of gray stone around the opening and hung a red bucket on a cord. My niece can lower the bucket almost to her elbow.

mbm-0415.clue: I always ask the bookshop for the brown paper.
mbm-0415.quote: I wrap a mystery novel and let my friend choose it by the first sentence I copy on the cover. She does the same for me. Our shelves have a whole little neighborhood of brown-paper houses.

mbm-0416.clue: I borrowed the tree’s catching hand.
mbm-0416.quote: Our flying disc lodged neatly across a fork in an old maple. From the ground it looked like the tree had made the cleanest catch of the match. We drew a little winner’s ribbon and tied it to a low branch.

mbm-0417.clue: I gave my pajamas a movie ticket.
mbm-0417.quote: I sewed the torn corner of an old ticket into the inside of my pajama pocket. It was from my mother’s favorite comedy. On movie night I always let her take the first handful of popcorn.
